description: Independent recomputation of implemented widgets by an external process, recorded after release. Release files are immutable once committed, so evidence about a release lives here and accrues as checks run. A parity result establishes numerical agreement with a named external implementation under a stated criterion. It is not scientific certification, and it says nothing about whether a method is appropriate for a question.

outcomes.agrees: Every case met the stated criterion.
outcomes.partial: Some cases met it and others did not; the measurement states which.
outcomes.diverges: The stated criterion was not met.
outcomes.unresolved: The comparison could not be made, for a reason the note gives.

entries.criterion: maximum separation below 0.001 m over the fixture points
entries.note: Recomputed from the declared PROJ definition rather than the source EPSG code, so the comparison tests what the widget says it did. Covers a projection change on one datum; no datum shift is exercised.

entries.criterion: identical opened window, included-cell set and retained values, per case
entries.measured: Cell-centre: agrees, 0 of 132 cells differ and retained values are identical. All-touched at a pixel-aligned cutline: 2 cells differ, both beside the alignment. All-touched with a one-pixel margin: the window differs and 61 cells differ, where the reference models the margin as a 3x3 binary dilation, which is not this widget's rule.
entries.note: Recorded per case rather than as one verdict. The two residual all-touched cells are what remains after adopting GDAL's positive-area rule, down from 35; see docs/experiments/29-raster-edge-inclusion.md. The margin case is an unresolved comparison, not an established defect: the reference and the widget define the margin differently.
